problems.issue: A4 and A7 were rendered and submitted before the owner's decision on rung 40 was recorded. The ladder stage handed that decision to Kevin explicitly and said to record it before A4 or A7 was rendered. D51 confirmed it about 13 hours later. Its reasoning is partly circular: it rules out a rung-40 rerun because a qualifying rerun after A7 would change N*, a situation that exists only because A7 had already run. Running A7 first closed off option (b), raising the limit and then rerunning rung 40, under attempt 1. Section 6.1 makes the rerun optional ('may be rerun once'), and with the host limit unchanged a rerun would almost certainly have failed the same way. So no verdict changes. This is a governance deviation, which the bundle discloses.

problems.issue: A4's PASS depended in part on not drawing a failure mode that is not in the action path and that no criterion bounds. A7 session 193 had a whole-boot /accessibility failure: HTTP 500 for the entire boot, no restart. Section 6.1 and D30/D33 excuse an undelivered tree only when a restart caused it. So the same event in any of A4's 534 accessibility-setting sessions would have failed A4 with about 59 counted failures, and only a repair attempt could rerun it, which cannot fix an upstream service. At the observed rate (1 in 1,245 accessibility boots) the chance that A4 avoided it was about 0.65; at the 95% upper bound it was about 0.13. The operator disclosed and quantified the event. This note adds the sensitivity of A4's verdict to it.

interpretation_notes: Every operator verdict reproduces from SHA-checked raw records using the frozen code and my own export: N* = 32 with rungs 8-32 qualifying; rung 40 did not count (it was not an abort); A1 at N* = 32 PASS; A4 PASS; A7 PASS; A5 (final) PASS. Together with stage A (C1-C4, A1 at N = 1, A2, A3, A6, verified independently before), the registered overall verdict holds. A1-A6 hold, so Stage 1 may start. A7 holds, so Stage-1 episodes may use the screenshot-plus-accessibility setting. N* < 40, so the program kill criterion applies: cut the Stage-1 task count before adding GPUs.

What the verdict licenses for Stage 1: the L0-fixed runtime and the two Stage-1 harness adapters (H-OSW-fixed, H-GA, on their in-spec cells), on this host as configured, at no more than 32 concurrent VMs, with 4 pinned CPUs per VM and the registered runner CPUs. What it does not license: concurrency above 32; another host, image or kernel configuration; catalog instances that were not tested; the guest server under Stage-1 task applications, whose accessibility trees are larger; or any per-entry claim at A4's level.

Per-class bounds A4 supports, with zero failures, at family-wise 95% (Bonferroni over 8 statements): the per-action failure rate of each of the seven classes, over the catalog's instances weighted as the plan weights them, is at most 4.97e-4 to 5.00e-4 (10,148-10,216 executed actions per class). The per-boot failure rate is at most 0.474% over 1,068 sessions. By the union bound, a 20-action episode loses at most about 1.47-1.5 pp to the action path. These bounds cover the L0-fixed runtime path, which is all A4 runs. Harness-adapter parsing has only A2 (10 repetitions per cell, both settings) and A3 (60 per stress entry). Per-entry bounds from A4 alone range from 4.2% for the 70-repetition mixed entries to 0.03% for move_only.

A7's restart bound: 0 guest-server restarts in 39,036 /accessibility calls at N = 32 on the probe desktop, an exact one-sided 95% upper bound of 7.67e-5 per call (5.8e-3 per session). That is well inside 5e-4. A7 bounds restarts only. It does not bound the observation service's other failures in this suite: a whole-boot HTTP 500 with no restart (1 in 1,245 accessibility boots, upper 95% 3.8e-3 per boot), two /accessibility hangs of about 125 s delivered on retry (2 in 91,800 calls), or a first-call HTTP 500 (15 sessions). Stage 1's preregistration should count undelivered observations, and possibly very slow ones, per episode, not only restarts, as the operator recommends.

Surprising: transient first-call 500s (19,672 or 19,689 bytes, about 1.5 s) appear only in the two long N = 32 campaigns: 4 of A4's 534 accessibility sessions and 11 of A7's 516. There were none in the 77 N = 1 accessibility sessions or the 118 ladder ones. That is too few to call it load-dependent, but Stage 1 should expect about 1-2% of accessibility boots to need a retry on their first observation. Session 193's 500 bodies are a different size (19,527 bytes) and much faster (0.1-0.3 s), so it was a different failure state. The response bodies were never recorded, so the cause is unknown.

Concurrency headroom is thin. The inotify limit (128 per user, shared by every root process on the host) let about 35 VM containers get dnsmasq. At N = 32 all 1,584 A4/A7 boots got NAT, but Stage 1 at 32 VMs runs about 3 containers below the failure point, and any other root inotify use on the host would erode that margin. N* = 32 also reflects a host configuration limit, not a measured runtime or timing limit: at N = 40, boot and step p95 (22.24 s; 3.17 s = 1.18 x N = 1) were within the limits, and the 4,200 trials that ran all passed.

Process: every campaign ran under attempt 1, exactly once. There was no rerun, no repair and no session split. Requeue=1 is still set in the lane, but Restarts=0 everywhere. The bundle's operator-computed figures (A1 at N*, the suite-wide undelivered-tree count, VM-hours, the per-class counts) all reproduce with my own code. The one governance weakness is that the rung-40 choice was made by an operator and ratified later in D51, rather than decided before A4/A7, as the ladder stage asked.
